name: studybridge
description: For tutors: Claude reads your learners’ work and progress in StudyBridge and drafts assignments, marking and messages for you to approve. For StudyBridge’s own content account: make and check content for students.
long_description: StudyBridge is a private tutoring portal. With this connector, Claude can see your learners, their submissions (including maths working and photos of their work), their progress, and the PDFs in your library. Claude can draft assignments, suggested marking with explanations, lessons and messages. Everything Claude makes is saved as a draft in StudyBridge → Prof, and reaches a learner only after you approve it. Learners never use Claude.

prompts.name: mark_latest
prompts.text: Using StudyBridge, look at the submissions waiting to be marked. For each one, read it carefully, then draft marks with clear explanations of any mistakes, and flag questions worth a redo.

prompts.name: weekly_report
prompts.text: Using StudyBridge, write me a short weekly report on each learner: time studied, work handed in, scores, strengths, topics that need work, and what to set next.

prompts.name: make_subject
prompts.description: Make StudyBridge content for a subject
prompts.text: Using StudyBridge’s content tools, help me make content for one subject. Start with content_overview and ask me which subject. Then: set its syllabus (the board’s topic names, in order, with codes and subtopics), write a lesson for each topic, about 10 practice questions per topic (mostly multiple choice and numbers, each with a hint and a worked solution), 10 flashcards per topic, and one original practice paper per paper of the real exam. Everything must be original: the same format, style and difficulty as the real exam, but never copied, reworded or adapted from a real past paper or a textbook.

prompts.name: check_waiting
prompts.description: Check waiting questions (in a new chat)
prompts.text: Using StudyBridge, check the questions waiting for their check. Call questions_to_check, solve every question yourself from scratch and carefully (don’t guess), and send your answers with submit_checks. If it asks you to compare written answers, say honestly with confirm_checks whether they mean the same. Repeat until nothing is waiting, then tell me how many passed and how many need me.
